# SignalTree

SignalTree is framework-neutral reactive application state with causal
semantics. The construction model is
`signalTree(initialState, { derived, enhancers })`; state is read through
`tree.$`.

## v16 Link declarations and native reader migration

`connection.declare(declaration, work)` declares complete inputs for synchronous
writes to its supported owned SignalTree source. Use `{ kind: 'independent' }`
only with no pending-owner inputs; `{ kind: 'dependent', owners: [pending] }`
for all contributing owners; `{ kind: 'unknown' }` when completeness is unknown.
Input owners do not acquire ownership of the callback's writes. Native evidence
still applies; hidden inputs, saved values and application-computed caches are
the application's completeness responsibility.

No async callback, returned thenable or declaration across await. Callback results
are discarded. Invalid declarations may throw after writes have occurred; those
writes can remain. `SignalTreePublicationError.stage` distinguishes
`before-callback` from `after-callback`; `reason` describes the rejection. Inspect
current state before recovery. This is not an atomic rollback wrapper.

`receipt.read()` is a current immutable admission snapshot, not a reactive signal
or delivery acknowledgment. `no-write` creates no new obligation and does not
approve or clear an existing one. Equal values can have different publication
support. `eligible`/`started` do not prove remote acceptance; even `settled()` can
resolve after endpoint failure reported through `onTreeError()`. After successful
dependency rejection, reevaluate current ordinary publication under current gates;
do not treat the old declaration as approved or expect the application recipe to
rerun. A surviving value may still publish.

Link only supported owned leaves, branches/roots, entity fields/rows/collections;
roots or branches containing EntityMap are excluded (link the collection itself).
Unowned callables and native computeds are not admitted just because their types
match. Use one framework facade consistently.

Native custom adapters with createWritableCell + createWritableProjection +
createReadonlyCell must add callable `createCurrentReadonlyCell(readCurrent)`.
It must lazily provide the promised native readonly carrier, stable identity,
tracking/cleanup and fresh values/errors on every direct read, including readers
retained before callbacks and nested writes. Missing capability rejects factory
construction before initial-state reads/tree allocation. Keep ordinary cached
readonly behavior; do not fake native carriers or flush application computeds.
Token-only/partial adapters keep portable routing. SignalTree-held reader freshness
does not change application-computed framework timing. These are v16 requirements;
stable v15 remains unchanged. See the kernel README for a declaration example.

## What SignalTree is — and is not

```text
IS:     framework-independent consequential application state, stable subject
      identity, authored versus external authority, coherent operation
      boundaries, causal/restoration semantics, and link-based relationships

IS NOT: primarily an undo library, event log, query library, sync engine, or
      persistence framework
```

Undo/redo, event replay, query composition, live synchronization, and
persistence are all things applications correctly BUILD on top of SignalTree's
causal model — see "Composition patterns" below — but none of them is what
SignalTree is FOR. Describe SignalTree by its primary job (consequential state
with a causal model an application can trust), not by one thing that model
happens to make easy.

Five packages ship under the hyphenated `@signal-tree/*` scope. The no-hyphen
`@signaltree/*` scope is the separate v14 line: still maintained for bug and
security fixes (currently `14.1.4`), frozen on features, and not an alias for
anything under `@signal-tree/*`. Generate `@signal-tree/*` names for new code:

- `@signal-tree/kernel` — framework-neutral tree, `entityMap()`, causal turns,
  links, and the `restoration()` / `transactions()` / `batching()` / `devTools()`
  enhancers. Also `@signal-tree/kernel/adapter`, the realization SDK.

  `tree.transact(fn)` opens an optimistic turn, settled with `confirm()` or
  `rollback()`. The handle also carries `inspect()`, which reports whether each
  change the turn made is still `'current'` or has been `'superseded'` — that is
  what a review screen renders, and the turn's values are readable immediately
  through ordinary references, so it renders from the state it already uses.
  There is ONE verb and ONE handle; no separate review API.

  A `rollback()` that cannot be proven safe REFUSES rather than guessing: it
  throws `SignalTreeRollbackError`, changes nothing, and leaves the transaction
  PENDING, so `confirm()` and a retried `rollback()` both stay available. Settle
  the NEWEST open transaction first; rolling an older one back while a newer
  overlapping one is open refuses with
  `cause.kind === 'later-confirmed-dependency'`. A newer pending transaction
  that omitted or re-added a branch enclosing the older one's writes counts as
  overlapping.
- `@signal-tree/angular` — the complete Angular application facade. **Angular
  code imports `signalTree` and all other SignalTree APIs from here**. Terminal
  state leaves are native `WritableSignal<T>` values and derived leaves are
  native `Signal<T>` values. Adds `defineStore()` and `toWritableSignal()` for
  adapting callable object branches or designating form ingress.
- `@signal-tree/react` — the complete React application facade. **React code
  imports `signalTree`, markers, enhancers, and `useSignalTree(owner, selector)`
  from here**; React observes the canonical kernel tree without copying it.
- `@signal-tree/vue` — the complete Vue application facade. **Vue code imports
  `signalTree` and all other SignalTree APIs from here**. Terminal state leaves
  are native `Ref<T>` values and derived leaves are `ComputedRef<T>` values.
- `@signal-tree/solid` — the complete Solid application facade. **Solid code
  imports `signalTree` and all other SignalTree APIs from here**. Leaves are
  real Solid accessors, so they are tracked by Solid's own reactivity rather
  than copied into it.

Use `@signal-tree/kernel` directly only for framework-neutral TypeScript,
including reusable domain libraries. Framework facades forward the neutral
kernel surface by canonical identity; they do not duplicate semantic authority.

## Current reads during callbacks (v16)

Root/object-branch snapshots and entity-projection readers consult current
installed state during callbacks, including readers acquired earlier. A retained
snapshot reader is not a historical snapshot: store its result to retain a value.

Native terminal leaves, application-created computed values, effects and React
renders retain framework publication timing. Snapshot freshness does not flush
those consumers. Read-after-write means after installation, not during
preparation before the write exists. Nested writes still follow the documented
whole-value ordering and omission rules; freshness does not change which later
writes win.

## Accessor grammar and terminal values

The neutral kernel exposes callable locations:

```typescript
location();                       // read
location(nextValue);              // replace the complete value
location((current) => nextValue); // derive the next complete value
```

The root (`tree.$`) and object branches keep this callable whole-value grammar
in every facade. Terminal values use the framework's native carrier:

```typescript
angularTree.$.count();
angularTree.$.count.set(5);
angularTree.$.count.update((count) => count + 1);

vueTree.$.count.value;
vueTree.$.count.value = 5;
```

React has no persistent signal primitive, so `@signal-tree/react` keeps neutral
locations and observes selected state through `useSignalTree(owner, selector)`.
EntityMap query and field leaves follow the same carrier rule; EntityMap command
methods such as `setAll()` and `updateOne()` do not change.

Plain objects normally become traversable branches. `leaf(value)` explicitly
ends topology so an object remains one atomic location. Declare function-valued
fields with `leaf(fn)`. At a callable write boundary, use `leaf(fn)` to distinguish
a stored function from an updater. Native Angular `.set(fn)` assigns the function
directly, as shown below:

```typescript
import { signalTree, leaf } from '@signal-tree/angular';
const angularTree = signalTree({
  range: leaf({ start: 0, end: 10 }),
  callback: leaf((value: number) => console.log(value)),
});

angularTree.$.range.set({ start: 5, end: 15 });
angularTree.$.callback.set((value) => console.log(value));
```

The wrapper is consumed at construction or invocation and never enters state,
snapshots, persistence, restoration, links, or causal payloads.

There is no v15 forms, persistence, validation, events, or realtime package;
those are application-owned. `.with()`, positional `derived`, and the
`stored`/`asyncSource`/`asyncQuery`/`form`/`status` markers were all removed.

## Migration Rule

Never design SignalTree around a legacy application's intermediate state.

1. Determine the canonical greenfield v15 architecture.
2. Implement and validate that architecture independently.
3. Migrate applications toward that target.
4. Prefer deleting obsolete concepts over adapting them.
5. Never add compatibility APIs merely to reduce migration work.
6. A migration may falsify the target architecture, but legacy usage does not
   define it.

Do not create intermediate APIs intended to be removed later. Do not add
compatibility layers because a migration is large. Do not preserve old
ownership because moving it is inconvenient. Do not design framework adapters
from legacy application idioms. Do not optimize for minimal migration diff.
Optimize for the architecture applications should use five years from now.

`@signal-tree/kernel/adapter` is the SDK for realization ownership, not a
compatibility layer. New exports must be framework-neutral semantic facts owned
by the kernel and required by correct realizations.

## Framework Realization Rule

Framework packages may realize SignalTree truth for their runtime. They must
not create another state authority.

Never use process-global mutable framework installation merely to make a legacy
integration work if construction-bound ownership can express the long-term
architecture. A migration cannot determine realization ownership.

## Framework Ownership Ratchet

`@signal-tree/kernel` owns framework-independent SignalTree semantics.
`@signal-tree/kernel/adapter` owns only neutral ports for semantic questions
the kernel owns. Framework packages own their implementations, lifecycle,
diagnostics, schedulers, rendering behavior, primitive identity rules, and
quirks. Neutral naming does not establish neutral ownership.

Every new realization contract must state its SignalTree semantic job, provide
a neutral implementation, be implementable by a tiny framework-free fake, and
name the kernel authority deciding when and why it runs. Reject contracts that
exist only for one framework. If Angular, React, and Vue disappeared, the
contract must remain meaningful to SignalTree or another reactive runtime.

## Composition patterns

Several capabilities that look like missing features are compositions of
primitives that already ship — see `docs/guides/composition-recipes.md` for
the full recipes with executable-spec citations. Do not propose a new marker
or kernel API for any of these before reading it:

- a standard enhancer policy, a reusable entity-CRUD Ops base, a selection
  read-model
- optimistic writes with server reconciliation (`transact()` and its
  pending/confirm/rollback lifecycle)
- agent or human review of changes before they land (`transact()` with
  `inspect()`, then `confirm()` or `rollback()`)
- staged/draft editing (an application-owned draft, one authored commit — no
  `beginStage()` session API)
- one-shot loading (`external()`, no `link()` needed for a single fetch) versus
  a persistent relationship with an external authority (`link()`'s three
  composable directions: PULL/PUSH-IN/PUSH-OUT)
- accepted external truth is distinct from authored application work, so an
  external write is not automatically a retained causal-history turn
- a human-readable explanation projected from the causal record (the
  explanation is a PROJECTION of causal truth — the kernel does not store
  prose, actor names, or timestamps merely to make one convenient)

`docs/guides/persistence-guide.md` is the `link()`-as-storage specialization
of the same model.

### Read-only runtime observation

Tooling can import `stateLocationReader`, `entityMembershipReader`,
`linkStateReader`, `transactionLifecycleReader` and `restorationReader` from
`@signal-tree/kernel/internals`. These observe the constructed tree; they do not
install enhancers or confer mutation/settlement authority. Use the appropriate
framework facade for application state, and reserve this entry point for tooling.

- `stateLocationReader` resolves structured property/entity addresses and current
  entity lifetimes. Do not parse dotted display paths as identity.
- `entityMembershipReader` exposes current collection membership and changes.
- `linkStateReader` observes Link state; local completion is not proof of remote
  durable persistence beyond the endpoint's contract.
- `transactionLifecycleReader` exposes pending transactions and settlement/refusal
  observations, including whether pending authority remains.
- `restorationReader` exposes history entries, recorded transaction lineage and undo/redo/jump outcomes.

Check optional-reader availability before use; readers do not enable missing
capabilities. Release subscriptions when the owning view/session ends, and destroy
owned trees at teardown. Readers are not a retained audit log.
`ConfirmedTurnEffectView.fieldSegments` preserves producer-known entity-field
address segments; `plainBranchMembership` distinguishes member presence before
and after an effect. Neither display paths nor an absent value can replace those
facts. Confirmed-history access remains subject to configured retention.
